frozen_commit_note: The commit that registers this file adds only this file and its README row.
question: How does the frozen system date diaries that carry a published date and that no step of its development used?
population: Every entry of the section 'Dated Diaries: Addenda' of ADART IV (printed pages 1 to 92; 46 entries, numbered -477 to -59) that has an English translation. ADsD does not hold these entries, and no rule, setting, test or audit of the system has read them. An entry that ADART IV calls a duplicate or a join of a text in ADART I to III is reported in a separate row.
published_year: The astronomical year of the entry number in its heading, so that No. -477 is year -477 (478/477 BCE), as in the benchmark. If the heading gives two years, the entry counts as included when its set holds either year.
input: Only the English translation, built and blinded by the rules that scripts/source/build_adart_iv_corpus.py applies to the undated diaries. The entry heading, museum number, date line, ruler and year cells, and the Date and Comments sections leave the input. A line that names a year, a king, a ruler or an era keeps only its parts after the first month heading that name none of these. The table of OCR corrections is not extended for this test.
dating: The rules of the frozen commit, applied once, in the way scripts/inference/date_adart_iv.py dates the undated entries. No rule, tolerance, parser rule, tier, window or setting changes after this registration.
new_code: Only an input builder for the addenda pages and a scorer. Neither may change how a clause is read, tested or scored.
scores: entries with a translation, and entries with at least one decisive clause
among entries with a decisive clause: inclusion of the published year in the first group and in the strict set
median sizes of the first group and of the strict set
commitments, and how many match the published year
reading: Descriptive. The rates are reported with their counts beside the benchmark rates (93% first group, 100% strict set). No threshold is set, because the test set is small.
after_scoring: An error found in the input builder after scoring is reported, and a corrected run is reported beside the first run, not in its place. No rule of the system changes because of the results.
